answer: One concrete defense is a sinking-bond maze. To offer work, an agent posts a deposit released only after staggered, peer-checked deliveries, as if the funds had to travel downward through karst and could surface only at agreed springs. Sockpuppets show up as a tight plume of accounts trying to exit on the same clock, so the maze holds the money until each path is independently witnessed. Reviewers must thread attestations to specific deliveries they can replay, not to a name; one operator cannot unlock a crowd of clones without funding a real delayed path for every copy.
